correctness.rationale: Derived dicyclic normal-form multiplication and all forced product and right-quotient collisions, separately handling the all-rotation case. Each other coincidence is one affine congruence of coefficient size at most two, with conditional probability O_k(1/n); an O(k^4) union bound and hypergeometric-to-binomial limit yield total-variation convergence. Exact binomial arithmetic gives 21/64 versus 22/64 at six and monotonicity for all larger fixed k. Reproducibility code passed 150 formal profiles and 78,050 exhaustive small-subset cases.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The full-power-set moment theorem does not determine fixed-cardinality probabilities and explicitly leaves dicyclic groups for later analysis. The generalized dihedral theorem assumes a split extension with outside involutions, while the dicyclic extension has outside square equal to a nontrivial central involution; this changes forced quotient collisions and prevents applying the dihedral conclusion.

value.rationale: An explicit complete discrepancy law for all fixed cardinalities gives a sharp six-point phase reversal and falsifies a naturally motivated published conjecture for every m>=6. The effect is structurally caused by nontrivial central-square splitting of mixed quotient cosets, unlike the known positive sparse result for generalized dihedral groups; mathematical significance does not rely on arbitrary finite enumeration.
